utility.notes: Albany is a well-documented Alameda County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: Ava Community Energy
value.notes: Ava Community Energy (formerly East Bay Community Energy) confirms Albany as a current member city, alongside Berkeley, Dublin, Emeryville, Fremont, Hayward, Livermore, Newark, Oakland, Piedmont, Pleasanton, San Leandro, and Union City in Alameda County. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

permit_authority.notes: The City's own Building page (albanyca.gov, migrated from the earlier albanyca.org domain) has a dedicated 'SolarApp+ and PV permits' section, found and directly read this session.

permit_url.notes: The City's site migrated from albanyca.org to albanyca.gov; the previous ecode360.com citation (S1) remains a valid municipal-code reference but is not the applicant-facing page. The FAQ/accordion content on this page (SolarApp+ and PV permits, Inspections) is rendered client-side and was extracted via direct DOM element lookup rather than visible-text scraping.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Albany/Alameda County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

City of Albany Building Permit Application

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'SolarApp+ and PV permits' page section. Projects not eligible for or not using SolarApp+ apply via email using the City's standard building-permit submittal process instead.

value: Schedule inspections by calling (510) 528-5760 or emailing permits@albanyca.org; next-day inspections are typically possible, but allow up to 3 days lead time
To cancel a scheduled inspection, call no later than 9:00am on the day of the inspection
A five-working-day advance notice may be required for a Final Inspection
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: The City's own page states 'Licensed Contractors can apply for PV permits and receive instant plan review for qualifying residential projects through SolarApp+' and refers to 'instant permit approval.'

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Rooftop Solar Systems streamlined permitting process (§12-14)
other_conditions: Streamlined process covers systems no larger than 10kW AC nameplate rating or 30kW thermal
Systems must meet applicable health and safety standards required by the State and the City of Albany Fire Department
Water-heating systems must be certified by an accredited listing agency per the California Building Standards Code
Electricity-producing systems must meet standards from the California Building Standards Code, IEEE, and accredited testing laboratories (e.g. UL)
Routine operation and maintenance does not require a permit

sources.title: § 12-14: Small Residential Rooftop Solar Systems; Streamlined Permitting Process
